note: Evals 1-5 and 7-13 run in a repo with no .agents/project.json and no tracker; eval 6 runs inside delivery on the profile of profiles/example.json.

evals.name: goal-to-overview
evals.prompt: on code ça ensemble : ajoute une fonction slugify dans utils avec ses tests
evals.expected_output: Says back in one line what will be true when done and how it is checked; gives the work overview (numbered steps, the decision in each, which ones stop, the end-to-end check); writes PLAN-<slug>.md outside the repo; waits for the go before any code; asks for no ticket, tracker or profile
assertions: The pair skill is used
Writes no repo code before the overview gate
Marks the steps that stop (a decision or a user-written piece)
Writes the plan file outside the repo, or asks once where the plans folder is
Asks for no ticket key, tracker or project profile

evals.name: default-branch
evals.prompt: (on the repo's default branch) pair avec moi sur le renommage du module billing
evals.expected_output: Creates a working branch before the first edit and says so; never commits on the default branch
assertions: Creates and switches to a working branch before editing
Says which branch it created

evals.name: plumbing-chains-stop-stops
evals.prompt: (overview agreed: steps 1 and 2 plumbing, step 3 a stop) go
evals.expected_output: Writes, tests and commits steps 1 and 2 without stopping, ticks them in the plan; writes step 3 with its GATE marker, runs its tests, leaves it uncommitted, opens the marker in the editor, explains in 2 to 4 points and ends with a stop block of three lines at most
assertions: Commits plumbing steps without stopping
Leaves the stop step uncommitted
Explains the step first in 2 to 4 points, each with what was done, where (file:line) and why
Ends with a stop block of at most three lines: step n/N and tests, each marker's file:line and decision, the expected answer

evals.name: ok-deletes-markers
evals.prompt: (stop step 3 written with a GATE marker, left uncommitted) ok
evals.expected_output: Deletes the marker itself, runs the tests, commits the step, ticks it, and chains to the next step
assertions: Deletes the marker itself on « ok »
Never commits a file holding a GATE or TODO pair marker
Commits the step and ticks it in the plan

evals.name: remark-as-edit
evals.prompt: (stop step 3 uncommitted; the user edited the function in the editor and wrote) j'ai changé l'arrondi, regarde
evals.expected_output: Reads git diff to pick up the user's edit, applies what it implies, runs the tests, and stops again only if the edit changed a decision
assertions: Reads git diff before answering
Runs the tests after the user's edit
Does not overwrite the user's edit

evals.name: called-from-delivery
evals.prompt: (delivery on SHOP-708, Decide done, decisions comment posted) go, on code
evals.expected_output: Delivery hands over to pair: the overview groups steps by PR and repo with the decision each one holds, the plan is PLAN-SHOP-708.md, the steps run in the ticket's worktrees, and Pre-QA's test data ids go in the ticket's notes file
assertions: Names the plan after the ticket key
Works in the ticket's worktrees, not the main checkouts
Hands back to delivery's Review and PR when done

evals.name: take-a-step
evals.prompt: (overview agreed, step 2 done, step 3 not started) à moi pour la 3
evals.expected_output: Writes what surrounds the piece, its signature with a TODO pair marker and a red test, runs the tests to show it red, leaves everything uncommitted, marks the step ✍ in the plan, says what the piece must do without saying how, and ends with the « à toi » block
assertions: Does not write the body of the piece
Leaves a signature with a TODO pair marker and a red test
Marks the step ✍ in the plan file
Ends with the « à toi » block: step n/N, the TODO's file:line and what to write, the three answers

evals.name: graded-hint
evals.prompt: (step 3 is the user's, TODO marker in place) indice
evals.expected_output: Gives the smallest hint that unblocks: where to look, with a file:line; no approach and no code until asked again
assertions: The first hint names where to look, with a file:line
Gives no code on the first ask
Writes nothing in the user's file

evals.name: review-the-users-code
evals.prompt: (step 3 is the user's; they wrote the body, one edge case is missed) fait
evals.expected_output: Reads git diff, runs the tests, says what the tests say first, then at most three remarks each with a file:line and what it costs; changes nothing in the user's code; stops on a remark that blocks, otherwise deletes the marker, commits and ticks
assertions: Reads git diff and runs the tests before answering
At most three remarks, each with a file:line and what it costs
Does not edit the user's code without being asked
Commits only once the marker is gone

evals.name: hand-back
evals.prompt: (step 3 is the user's, TODO marker in place, body not written) prends-la
evals.expected_output: Writes the body itself, turns the step into a stop step with a GATE marker on what it chose, and ends with the usual stop block
assertions: Writes the body and replaces the TODO marker with a GATE marker on its choice
Leaves the step uncommitted and ends with the stop block

evals.name: unplanned-stop
evals.prompt: (overview agreed on the assumption that settings.FEE_FLOOR is one number; a teammate's commit made it a per-currency table) go
evals.expected_output: Stops where the assumption breaks, commits nothing of the step, and says in four lines at most: the step, what was assumed, what was found with its file:line, the options with a recommendation; updates the plan on the answer before carrying on
assertions: Does not pick an option silently
Names what the plan assumed and what the code holds, with a file:line
Offers options with a recommendation
Updates the plan file once the user answers

evals.name: preference-proposed
evals.prompt: (the learner notes say the user writes the tests themselves) on code ça ensemble : ajoute la remise par volume
evals.expected_output: Reads the learner notes before the overview; proposes ✍ on the test steps and says why; the user still agrees or moves the marks at the gate
assertions: Reads the learner notes before the overview
Marks the test steps ✍ and says it comes from the notes
Still asks the user to agree on who writes what

evals.name: notes-after-the-job
evals.prompt: (the job is done; the user wrote `fee_for` and its review had no blocking remark)
evals.expected_output: Updates the learner notes before the closing message: the zone becomes solide with the date and the fact that the user wrote it and it passed review
assertions: Marks the zone solide with the date and the evidence
Writes no judgement of the person
